items.title: 67559_Art Hodes oral history interview
items.q: And between Dick and I we had six dollars... And the band, the trio was there... It's just you today.

ctx.x: Grasso who later did some things with us. I'm not sure, but I think so. But in any case, the drummer had an uncle who was a union delegate. So he had some clout. And he told us not to worry about nothing, we were safe.

But the pay was a big, fat $18 for six nights, three dollars a night, which we needed because we had nothing. And between Dick and I we had six dollars. And wine at 25 cents a bottle, you could see we could get by and not be too --. Well, about the fourth day, I came to work and I noticed they were picketing the place. My union was picketing the place. I says, oh, I can't, this is too much and I need the money. What are they doing? So when the picket separated and went in opposite directions, I put my -- at that…

And the band, the trio was there, and they told me not to worry again. Everybody tells me not to worry. But so that night -- it was just a question of running between the pickets. But either the next night or the night after, it didn't really matter, because the boss had let the whole band go. I came to work, I looked up and I said to the boss, where's the band? He says, there is no band. I says, what happened? He says, well, I had to let them go. It's just you today.
